steps.message:
I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Today is Saturday, October 24, 2026. Submissions close six days from today, on Friday, at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The deadline is Friday, October 30, 2026, at 11:59 PM PT.

1.  **Time Zone Offset**: On October 30, 2026, the US Pacific Time zone is still in Daylight Saving Time (PDT, UTC-7), as it doesn't transition to PST until November 1.
2.  **Madrid Offset**: Spain transitions from CEST (UTC+2) to CET (UTC+1) on the last Sunday of October, which is October 25, 2026. Therefore, on October 30, Madrid is in CET (UTC+1).
3.  **Time Difference**: The difference between UTC-7 and UTC+1 is 8 hours.
4.  **Calculation**: 11:59 PM on October 30 + 8 hours = 7:59 AM on October 31.

ANSWER: 2026-10-31 07:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Today is Friday, October 30, 2026. The form closes this coming Monday at 10:00 AM Los Angeles time."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The current date provided is Friday, October 30, 2026. "This coming Monday" refers to November 2, 2026.

To determine the time difference between Los Angeles and Madrid on November 2, 2026:
1. **Los Angeles Time:** In the US, Daylight Saving Time ends on the first Sunday of November. In 2026, this is Sunday, November 1. Therefore, on Monday, November 2, Los Angeles will be on Pacific Standard Time (PST), which is UTC-8.
2. **Madrid Time:** In Spain, Daylight Saving Time ends on the last Sunday of October. In 2026, this is Sunday, October 25. Therefore, on Monday, November 2, Madrid will be on Central European Time (CET), which is UTC+1.
3. **Calculation:** The difference between UTC-8 and UTC+1 is 9 hours.
4. **Conversion:** 10:00 AM (Los Angeles) + 9 hours = 19:00 (Madrid).

ANSWER: 2026-11-02 19:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The hackathon starts Saturday, October 24, 2026 at 18:00 Madrid time and lasts exactly 48 hours."
When is the end of the hackathon in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The hackathon starts on Saturday, October 24, 2026, at 18:00 Madrid time (CEST, UTC+2). 

In Spain, the transition from Central European Summer Time (CEST) to Central European Time (CET) occurs on the last Sunday of October. In 2026, this transition takes place on Sunday, October 25, when clocks move back one hour at 03:00 CEST to 02:00 CET.

Because of this "extra" hour gained during the DST switch, 48 elapsed hours from Saturday at 18:00 will result in a local time that is one hour earlier than the starting wall-clock time.

Calculation:
1. Start: Oct 24, 18:00 CEST (UTC+2).
2. 48 hours later: Oct 26, 16:00 UTC.
3. Local time in Madrid on Oct 26: CET (UTC+1).
4. 16:00 UTC + 1 hour = 17:00 CET.

ANSWER: 2026-10-26 17:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The final round starts October 26, 2026 at 10:00 AM PT; submissions close exactly 72 hours later."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The contest starts on October 26, 2026, at 10:00 AM PT. On this date, the US is still observing Pacific Daylight Time (PDT, UTC-7). Meanwhile, Spain switches from Central European Summer Time (CEST) to Central European Time (CET, UTC+1) on Sunday, October 25, 2026. Therefore, on October 26 and 29, Madrid will be in CET (UTC+1).

The time difference between PDT (UTC-7) and CET (UTC+1) is 8 hours.
Start time in Madrid: October 26, 10:00 AM + 8 hours = 18:00 (6:00 PM).
The deadline is 72 hours (exactly 3 days) after the start.
Deadline in Madrid: October 26, 18:00 + 72 hours = October 29, 18:00.

ANSWER: 2026-10-29 18:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close October 31, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET. Results are announced exactly 36 hours after submissions close."
When is the results announcement in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close October 31, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET. Results are announced exactly 36 hours after submissions close."
When is the results announcement in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

To determine the announcement time in Madrid, we first establish the timeline in UTC to avoid confusion with Daylight Saving Time changes.

1.  **Submission Close Time:** October 31, 2026, at 11:59 PM ET. On this date, the US is still in Eastern Daylight Time (EDT), which is UTC-4.
    *   UTC time: October 31, 23:59 + 4 hours = **November 1, 03:59 UTC**.

2.  **Announcement Time:** The results are announced exactly 36 hours later.
    *   November 1, 03:59 UTC + 36 hours = **November 2, 15:59 UTC**.

3.  **Convert to Madrid Time:** In Spain, Daylight Saving Time (CEST) ends on the last Sunday of October. In 2026, this occurs on October 25. Therefore, by November 2, Madrid is on Central European Time (CET), which is UTC+1.
    *   November 2, 15:59 UTC + 1 hour = **November 2, 16:59**.

ANSWER: 2026-11-02 16:59

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Deadline (Unix timestamp, seconds): 1791788340."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

To determine the deadline in Tokyo local time, we first convert the Unix timestamp to UTC and then adjust for the Tokyo time zone (UTC+9).

1.  **Convert Unix timestamp to UTC**:
    *   The Unix timestamp is 1,791,788,340 seconds.
    *   Seconds in a day: $86,400$.
    *   Total days since the Epoch (1970-01-01): $1,791,788,340 \div 86,400 \approx 20,738.2912$ days.
    *   Days from 1970-01-01 to 2026-01-01: $(56 \text{ years} \times 365) + 14 \text{ leap days} = 20,454$ days.
    *   Days into 2026: $20,738 - 20,454 = 284$ full days elapsed.
    *   The 285th day of 2026 is October 12th (January 31 + February 28 + March 31 + April 30 + May 31 + June 30 + July 31 + August 31 + September 30 = 273 days; $285 - 273 = 12$).
    *   Remaining seconds for the time: $1,791,788,340 \pmod{86,400} = 25,140$ seconds.
    *   $25,140 \text{ seconds} = 6 \text{ hours}, 59 \text{ minutes}, 0 \text{ seconds}$.
    *   UTC Time: **2026-10-12 06:59**.

2.  **Convert UTC to Tokyo local time (UTC+9)**:
    *   $06:59 + 9 \text{ hours} = 15:59$.
    *   Date remains October 12, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-10-12 15:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 2026-10-25T02:30:00Z."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The deadline is given in UTC (indicated by the "Z"). Madrid, Spain, follows Central European Time. On October 25, 2026 (the last Sunday of October), Spain transitions from Central European Summer Time (CEST, UTC+2) to Central European Time (CET, UTC+1). The clock change occurs at 03:00 CEST, which is 01:00 UTC, at which point the time reverts to 02:00 CET. Since the deadline of 02:30 UTC occurs after this transition, Madrid will be in CET (UTC+1). Therefore, 02:30 UTC + 1 hour = 03:30 local time.

ANSWER: 2026-10-25 03:30

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close at 11:59 PM Pacific Time on the last Sunday of October 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The last Sunday of October 2026 is October 25. At that time, Pacific Time is still in Pacific Daylight Time (PDT, UTC-7), as the US does not switch to Standard Time until November. Madrid, Spain, switches from Central European Summer Time (CEST, UTC+2) to Central European Time (CET, UTC+1) on that same day, October 25.

1.  Deadline: October 25, 2026, at 11:59 PM PDT (UTC-7).
2.  Convert to UTC: October 26, 2026, at 06:59 AM UTC.
3.  Convert to Madrid time: Since Madrid is in CET (UTC+1) on October 26, the time is 07:59 AM.

ANSWER: 2026-10-26 07:59

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Deadline: 12:00 noon Eastern Time on the day the US ends daylight saving time in 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The United States ends daylight saving time on the first Sunday of November. In 2026, that date is November 1. At 2:00 AM on that day, Eastern Daylight Time (UTC-4) reverts to Eastern Standard Time (UTC-5). Since the deadline is 12:00 noon, the applicable time zone is EST (UTC-5). Lima, Peru, is always in Peru Time (UTC-5). Therefore, 12:00 noon EST is the same as 12:00 noon in Lima.

ANSWER: 2026-11-01 12:00

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Deadline: December 31, 2026, 24:00 AoE."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

AoE (Anywhere on Earth) corresponds to the time zone UTC-12.

1.  The deadline is December 31, 2026, at 24:00 UTC-12.
2.  To convert UTC-12 to UTC, add 12 hours: January 1, 2027, 12:00 UTC.
3.  Tokyo, Japan is in JST (UTC+9). To convert UTC to JST, add 9 hours: January 1, 2027, 21:00 JST.

ANSWER: 2027-01-01 21:00

I live in Madrid, Spain, but that week I'm traveling in New York, USA, and I need New York time. A contest page says: "The deadline is 5:00 PM Sydney time on October 5, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Sydney, Australia, observes Australian Eastern Daylight Time (AEDT, UTC+11) starting the first Sunday of October. In 2026, the first Sunday is October 4, so on October 5, Sydney is UTC+11. New York observes Eastern Daylight Time (EDT, UTC-4) in October.

The time difference is 15 hours (11 - (-4) = 15). 
Subtracting 15 hours from 5:00 PM (17:00) on October 5 results in 2:00 AM on the same day.

ANSWER: 2026-10-05 02:00
